correctness.rationale: All 56 exceptional divisor classes are explicitly enumerated, with exact pair counts (756 disjoint pairs, 756 unit intersections, 28 double intersections) and a Geiser permutation preserving the 812-edge weighted graph. The integral involution matrix on the degree-zero divisor lattice and the quotient presentations [M | T−I] and [M | T+I] are derived. The standard perfect invariant monodromy pairing identifies their duals with fixed/anti-fixed kernels. Standard-library verifier reconstructs four different 55x55 rooted Laplacians, independent exact Bareiss determinants, root-independent prime-local Smith factors at p=2,5,7 with precision exceeding the determinant valuations. The displayed direct sums match those exact factors. Geometry-to-Neron claim is explicitly conditional; no finite test is promoted to an infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: The exact nonequivariant Smith group of the same 56-curve weighted graph is prior and is not asserted as new. Knowing abstract K or the rational spectrum does not determine the action of its Geiser involution, hence cannot imply the two integral eigensubgroups. Relevant graph-cover and dihedral-action theorems provide machinery but do not tabulate or force these specific local invariant factors without the new explicit calculation. No exact match was identified in the checked primary literature or mathematical search records; older unindexed work remains a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: A specialist computation of the Geiser-involution graph Jacobian could exist under antipodal, signed-graph or component-group terminology without searchable indexing.
A general signed graph-covering theorem may furnish an alternate computation, but no checked statement was found that already evaluates these exact groups.
The conditional Neron realization requires a nodal full boundary and an actual equivariant regular semistable smoothing, which the theorem does not independently construct.

value.rationale: The Geiser involution is the intrinsic anticanonical deck involution, not a selected arbitrary graph symmetry. Its fixed component group governs natural quadratic descent questions; its anti-fixed component group is the complementary geometric invariant. The theorem distinguishes complete five-primary anti-invariance and a nontrivial prime-two failure of integral direct-sum splitting; neither is implied by the previously known nonequivariant group or rational spectrum. This is substantive information about an intrinsic del Pezzo boundary.
